### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.completion

### Description

Currently mini.nvim does not include `completionContext` info in the request params:

https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#completionContext

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the suggestion!

I have seen this in the specification, but deliberately omitted adding this as I couldn't find a use case for this. Could you, please, elaborate about the use case for which this would make a difference?

Thanks for sharing the update!

I don't find a very valid use case for this, so it is completely up to you for whether you decide to implement it. Since `completionContext` is an optional field in the LSP specification, so there should be no problem for not providing this.

One usecase (though not very important) is that I implemented an [in-process LSP](https://github.com/milanglacier/minuet-ai.nvim) for AI based code completion. For AI based code completion, given the generation speed and rate limits, so it is not ideal to trigger it too frequently, especially trigger it during partial word input. So by passing `triggerCharacters`, then this in-process LSP should be able to only process completion request when the completion is triggered by `triggerCharacters`.

But I do agree that this is not an important issue. Because in LSP 3.18 protocol there is a new request method `inlineCompletion` which seems to be more suited for AI based completion. Though I know there are still people who prefer using the popup menu instead of ghost text for AI completion (based on the user base of copilot-cmp and codeium, and `ai_cmp` enabled by default in lazyvim).

**Off topic**: There is also an off topic thing: I personally think that it is a pity that there is no way for LSP to determine whether a completion is manually triggered by user or automatically triggered. As `Invoked` kind is documented as either triggered manually or by API. As a result, when a client makes an auto completion request that is not triggered by `triggerCharacter`, then it should use `Invoked` as trigger kind, this is also what nvim-cmp or blink will use during their completion session.
Hmmm... That's an interesting use case. Thanks for sharing! I'll take a closer look here.

Thanks for the update!

 To be honest I really wish there is a triggerkind in the LSP specification to determine whether the completion is manually invoked by the user. I feel that would be much more useful in my use case (for AI based completion).

It is also interesting that the `triggerkind` specification of the `inlineCompletion`  now includes a `manual` field. But there isn’t the counterpart for the `Completion triggerKind`.

I guess Microsoft didn’t think there are people who prefer using popup menu for AI-based completion from the beginning of the design.

> @231tr0n  One solution could be using `on_attach` inside a `for` loop. For example:  
> 
> ```lua
> local lspconfig = require('lspconfig')
> 
> local function on_attach(client, _)
>     if client.server_capabilities.completionProvider then
>         client.server_capabilities.completionProvider.resolveSupport = {
>             properties = { "documentation", "detail" }
>         }
>     end
> end
> 
> local servers = { "gopls", "tsserver", "lua_ls", "pyright" } -- Add your LSP servers here
> 
> for _, server in ipairs(servers) do
>     lspconfig[server].setup {
>         on_attach = on_attach,
>     }
> end
> ```
> This ensures that all configured LSP servers enable `documentation` and `detail` for completion items automatically.

Hi. What I wanted to convey was that since mini.completion supports hover window for showing docs, it would be better if this was added by default to mini.completion.

> @231tr0n  One solution could be using `on_attach` inside a `for` loop. For example:

> ```lua
> local lspconfig = require('lspconfig')
>

>         }
>     end
> end
> 
> local servers = { "gopls", "tsserver", "lua_ls", "pyright" } -- Add your LSP servers here
> 
> for _, server in ipairs(servers) do
>     lspconfig[server].setup {
>         on_attach = on_attach,
>     }
> end
> ```
> This ensures that all configured LSP servers enable `documentation` and `detail` for completion items automatically.

Also the reason why I declare them seperately instead of putting them in a for loop is because of inlay hints which has different config for different servers

> > Also the reason why I declare them seperately instead of putting them in a for loop is because of inlay hints which has different config for different servers
> 
> @231tr0n You can configure each server individually while still using a loop for general settings. For example:  
> 
> ```lua
> local lspconfig = require('lspconfig')
> 
> local function on_attach(client, _)
>     if client.server_capabilities.completionProvider then
>         client.server_capabilities.completionProvider.resolveSupport = {
>             properties = { "documentation", "detail" }
>         }
>     end
> end
> 
> local servers = {
>     gopls = {
>         settings = {
>             gopls = { hints = { assignVariableTypes = true } }
>         }
>     },
>     tsserver = {},
>     lua_ls = {},
>     pyright = {},
> }
> 
> for server, config in pairs(servers) do
>     config.on_attach = on_attach
>     lspconfig[server].setup(config)
> end
> ```
> 
> > Hi. What I wanted to convey was that since mini.completion supports hover window for showing docs, it would be better if this was added by default to mini.completion.
> 
> I'm sure I saw that you had already added this in `mini.completion` in some parts of the issues and that it was already resolved. But let's see what @echasnovski  says.
> 
> 

This seems interesting. Will try to do it this way. Thanks for letting me know.

> [@echasnovski](https://github.com/echasnovski) ! I just wanted to ask as part of this issue, is it possible to enable documentation and detail support for completion items. I currently use the below snippet and pass it to every server manually. This enables doc for all completion items for jdtls.

It has nothing to do with this issue. What you describe is automatically advertise client capabilities to servers (which 'mini.completion' doesn't do, at the moment at least), while this issue is about doing something directly inside 'mini.completion' request. The reason for this is mostly because I didn't realize that server's supplied data can drastically change depending on that information. Also I don't see a clean way to do that other than something like a new `make_lsp_capabilities()`. I'll maybe take a look at that.

This should now be resolved on latest `main`. The `textDocument/completion` request now sends proper context. @milanglacier, unfortunately, it does follow the LSP spec and provides `Invoked` for when the user manually triggers completion. But hope it'll still help with your plugin.

Also I don't see a clean way to do that other than something like a new `make_lsp_capabilities()`. I'll maybe take a look at that.

@echasnovski! Will this new make_lsp_capabilities function be implemented as well?

> [@echasnovski](https://github.com/echasnovski)! Will this new make_lsp_capabilities function be implemented as well?

Yes, I am going to take a look at the best course of action here. The most problematic part for me is how to document it and its usage in the most forward-compatible way (so ideally without using other plugins) possible.

I'll also take a look at pros and cons of doing similar to what ['Saghen/blink.cmp' is doing](https://github.com/Saghen/blink.cmp/blob/52cd2aae77db635af85d6e642fe19c56782c0e5c/plugin/blink-cmp.lua#L2-L4) with the Neovim>=0.11 built-in LSP configs.

> The textDocument/completion request now sends proper context. @milanglacier, unfortunately, it does follow the LSP spec and provides Invoked for when the user manually triggers completion. But hope it'll still help with your plugin.

Thanks for the update! I think you mean `Invoked` is provided when the completion is triggered by the keyword length (like typing a non-trigger character). I completely understand that as we should follow the LSP spec to avoid potential conflict with broader scope LSP servers.

> I think you mean `Invoked` is provided when the completion is triggered by the keyword length (like typing a non-trigger character).

Both (as per spec "Completion was triggered by typing an identifier (24x7 code complete), manual invocation (e.g Ctrl+Space) or via API."), which the point of off-topic in [this comment](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/issues/1694#issuecomment-2746730710).

> [@echasnovski](https://github.com/echasnovski)! Will this new make_lsp_capabilities function be implemented as well?

@231tr0n, 'mini.completion' now has [`get_lsp_capabilities()`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/9af69d8c655e609a7eb043e8f9c27530580d4838/doc/mini-completion.txt#L412) function. Thanks for bringing attention to the issue of properly advertising 'mini.completion' capabilities as LSP client.

For reference:
- On Neovim>=0.11 for LSP servers that are enabled via `vim.lsp.enable()` [this config](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/9af69d8c655e609a7eb043e8f9c27530580d4838/doc/mini-completion.txt#L419) should be enough.
- For 'nvim-lspconfig':

    ```lua
    local capabilities = require('mini.completion').get_lsp_capabilities()
    require('lspconfig').server_name.setup({ capabilities = capabilities })
    ```
